blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running warehouse operations well is not a matter of talent — it is a matter of standards. Every task, from receiving to picking, packing and dispatch, must have a clear way to do it. That method should be written down, short enough to read in five minutes, and followed by everyone on the floor. Variation is the enemy: when two pickers do the same job in two different ways, the error rate doubles for no good reason.

Standards work because they free the team from deciding small things over and over again. They also catch mistakes quickly. If a parcel is labelled the wrong way, anyone can see at once that the standard was not followed, and the problem is fixed before it reaches the customer.

Warehouses that run on clear standards feel calm, even on the busiest days. Warehouses that rely on individual cleverness feel exciting — and exhausting — and they lose people fast.

items.q: According to the text, running warehouse operations well depends mainly on…
options: the speed of the dispatch team
items.why: "Running warehouse operations well… is a matter of standards."

items.q: Why does the error rate double when two pickers do the same job differently?
options: Because the parcels are too heavy
Because variation itself creates avoidable mistakes
Because the customers change their orders
items.why: "Variation is the enemy… the error rate doubles for no good reason."

items.q: How do standards help catch mistakes, according to the text?
options: They make the team work more slowly
They reduce the number of parcels handled
They make a broken rule immediately visible to everyone
They remove the need for supervisors
items.why: "anyone can see at once that the standard was not followed."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Doing the same task two different ways raises the error rate
A warehouse should reward clever, improvised solutions on the floor
Calm operations are a sign of good standards
A short written method is easier to follow than a long one
items.why: Inferência: o texto associa a 'esperteza individual' ao cansaço e à perda de gente — o autor não a recomenda.

items.q: The final paragraph suggests that a warehouse which feels "exciting" is probably…
options: hard to sustain and likely to lose staff
items.why: Inferência: 'exciting — and exhausting — and they lose people fast' liga a emoção ao desgaste e à rotatividade.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily explicando por que está escrevendo um padrão de embalagem. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, I spent an hour on the packing line this morning, and I watched three different pickers pack exactly the same box in three completely different ways. Same product, same order — three methods. That is the whole problem in one picture.

Here is why it matters. One of them didn't tape the base twice, and that box is the one most likely to open in transit. Another labelled the parcel on the side instead of the top, so the scanner at dispatch had to be turned by hand. None of that is anyone's fault — nobody ever wrote the method down.

So I'm writing a one-page standard. Not a manual — one page. Every packer must read it before their next shift, and they have to follow it exactly, even when we're busy. Supervisors need to check the first few boxes each morning, just to be sure.

I know a written rule feels slow at first. But once everyone packs the same way, we stop arguing about it, the error rate drops, and honestly the whole floor gets calmer. That's the point — calm beats exciting in here.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did Emily see on the packing line this morning?
options: A scanner that had stopped working
Three pickers refusing to follow the manual
Three pickers packing the same box in three different ways
items.why: "I watched three different pickers pack exactly the same box in three completely different ways."

items.q: According to Emily, why did the scanner at dispatch have to be turned by hand?
options: The label was put on the side instead of the top
The box was too heavy to lift
The base was not taped twice
items.why: "Another labelled the parcel on the side instead of the top, so the scanner… had to be turned by hand."

items.q: How does Emily describe the document she is writing?
items.why: "I'm writing a one-page standard. Not a manual — one page."

items.q: When Emily says "None of that is anyone's fault," she most likely means…
options: the mistakes are too small to matter
the real problem is the missing written method, not the people
items.why: Inferência: ela liga logo em seguida — 'nobody ever wrote the method down' — culpando a ausência do padrão, não as pessoas.

items.q: What does Emily expect the written standard to achieve in the end?
options: A calmer floor and a lower error rate
items.why: Inferência: 'the error rate drops… the whole floor gets calmer… calm beats exciting.'

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every packer follows the same standard, so the boxes look identical." A standard is…
options: a senior manager on the floor
an agreed, fixed way of doing something
items.why: Standard = padrão: a maneira acordada e fixa de fazer a tarefa.

items.q: "When two people do the job differently, the error rate doubles." The error rate is…
options: the speed of the packing line
the number of workers on shift
items.why: Error rate = taxa de erros: a frequência com que as falhas ocorrem.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A clear standard removes ___ , so every parcel is packed the same way."
items.why: Variation = variação: é justamente o que o padrão elimina.

items.q: "Please label the box on the top, not on the side." To label means to…
options: attach a mark or tag showing what it is
items.why: To label = etiquetar: colocar a marca/etiqueta que identifica o pacote.

items.q: "A good standard frees the team from deciding small things over and over." Here, to free means to…
options: release someone from a burden or task
give the team a day off
items.why: To free = liberar: tirar do time o peso de redecidir cada detalhe.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem na operação do armazém. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The supervisor has to sign off on the new packing standard before it goes live." To sign off on means to…
options: read it out loud to the team
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new standard to every shift next Monday." To roll out means to…
options: put it into use across the operation
items.why: Roll out = implementar, colocar em uso de forma ampla.

items.q: "A couple of packers pushed back on the new rule, saying their old way was faster." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo.

items.q: "Emily agreed to write the standard, and this time she followed through." She…
options: asked someone else to do it
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Taping the base twice really does cut down on boxes opening in transit." To cut down on means to…
items.why: Cut down on = reduzir a quantidade ou frequência de algo.
